title: Detect prefetch/warmup oscillation and autotune alerting
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: We see frequent alert flapping and noisy SLO violations tied to prefetch/prefix warmup behavior on some routes. Short warmup bursts (a few requests) cause token-cost spikes and immediate alerts which then resolve, creating false positives and oncall fatigue. This PR introduces a lightweight oscillation detector and an alert-autotune pipeline that dampens alerts during transient warmup cycles while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.

What changed: added a new metric obs_prefetch_warmup_factor computed as a rolling-derivative of per-route prefix-token-cost normalized by steady-state cost; added obs_prefetch_oscillation_score (0..1) with exponential smoothing and hysteresis; introduced an alert-autotune service that adjusts per-tenant/per-route alert thresholds for token-cost and p95 latency during detected oscillation windows (configurable decay/backoff). Instrumentation: Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry spans for the detector pipeline, and structured log enrichment for sampled invocations (prefetch_sample_id). Dashboard: new 'Prefetch Warmup Oscillation' dashboard with heatmap, per-route time-series, and a canary panel that shows before/after adjusted thresholds.

Checklist (done): - metric + exporter (prometheus) added and validated against synthetic replay harness - OTEL spans with attributes pref_prefetch_score, detector_window_ms - logging hooks to attach sample keys (prefetch_sample_id) for downstream synthetic debugging - dashboard JSON + runbook link - unit + integration tests for detector and autotune engine - migration: a feature-flag gate (obs.prefetch_osc) default off for 48h ramp in main production clusters

Operational notes: the autotune applies a conservative multiplier (0.75..1.25) and uses a min-duration of 3 minutes and max-duration of 30 minutes for any single autotune action. We also record audit events (obs.autotune.audit) to allow manual rollback. The runbook (linked) describes how to disable the feature flag and how to inspect sample invocations from the dashboard.

Why this is safe: changes are behind a gate, autotune only adjusts alert thresholds (not traffic), and the detector is read-only on metrics. We added an audit trail and rate-limited actions to avoid runaway behavior.

Related: Linear ENG-3245 (prefetch stability), ENG-3278 (alert fatigue follow-up). Runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3245/prefetch-oscillation-runbook.
